hooks.prompt: Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if you are currently operating as a TESTER (writing and running tests with vitest/playwright). If you are NOT in a testing role (e.g. you are an engineer, grader, or debugger), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this restriction only applies to testing sessions. If you ARE the tester, check: testers must NOT destroy production source or publish packages. BLOCK: rm targeting src/, lib/, routes/, components/ (non-test directories), git push --force (allow --force-with-lease), git reset --hard, git clean -f, npm/pnpm/yarn publish, shell output redirection to production source files (.svelte, .ts, .js in src/ or lib/ — excluding .test. and .spec. files), dd/mkfs/shred. ALLOW: vitest, playwright, npm install, git push (non-force), rm in test directories, all read commands. Respond {"ok": true} if the command is safe for a tester, or {"ok": false, "reason": "BLOCKED: Testers must not destroy production source"} if blocked.

Review this test file for quality issues. Context: $ARGUMENTS. Check for: 1) Svelte 4 patterns in test setup (on:click, export let, createEventDispatcher, slot, $: reactive) — these are FORBIDDEN, use Svelte 5 runes only ($state, $derived, $effect, $props). 2) Implementation-detail testing (spying on internal state, asserting internal method calls rather than observable behavior). 3) Missing behavior assertions (test body has no meaningful expect() or assert calls — only stubs or TODOs). 4) Hardcoded timeouts (setTimeout/sleep waits instead of waitFor/findBy async queries). 5) TypeScript 'any' types or missing type annotations in test files. Respond {"ok": true} or {"ok": false, "reason": "specific violation with line context"}.

Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if this session involved writing or running tests. If NO test files were created, modified, or executed in this session (e.g. this was a grading, engineering, or debugging session), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this hook only applies to testing sessions. If tests WERE written or run, verify: 1) All requested test files were written and saved (not just planned). 2) Written test files contain meaningful assertions — not just TODO stubs or empty describe blocks. 3) All written tests were executed at least once and their pass/fail status is known and reported to the user. 4) If a coverage target (80%) was specified or checked, coverage was analyzed and the result was reported. 5) No test files contain Svelte 4 patterns (on:click event handlers, export let prop declarations, createEventDispatcher, slot elements, $: reactive declarations) — only Svelte 5 runes are allowed. 6) All test files use TypeScript (lang='ts' in svelte test setup, or .ts file extension). Respond {"ok": true} if all criteria are met, or {"ok": false, "reason": "description of what remains incomplete"} to force continuation.
